$description: LAYER 3 — SEMANTIC. Named jobs: surfaces, text, borders, interaction, attention, verdict marks, state expression, typography roles, spacing tiers, sizing, radius, elevation, motion, stacking layers and layout. A semantic token references PRIMITIVE tokens only. The single exception is color.signal.attention, which references brand.color.gold, because the attention signal is one of gold's three jobs (Constitution Article 12 §2). Verdict, state and interaction tokens never reach brand. Colour tokens resolve per GROUND; a null value means the role does not exist on that ground and is emitted as `initial`, so it cannot be used there. These are the only tokens emitted as CSS variables (`--lumi-*`).

$environments.$description: Product-context environments (PR-9). Chosen by route family and by controlled marketing sections, never by the viewer. There is no theme switch, no prefers-color-scheme branch and no user preference.

marketing-dark-section.description: A controlled Charcoal section inside marketing. The only place a verdict or the attention signal may appear on a marketing page (Constitution Article 13).

surface.$description: Surface roles (Constitution Article 16). Light encodes importance, not physical height: 'raised' is one step of light for a reading region, and 'elevated' is the only surface that sits above content (menus, popovers, dialogs; paired with shadow.overlay).

raised.$description: A reading region distinct from the ground.

elevated.$description: An overlay above content. On Off White it keeps the ground value and is separated by shadow.overlay and color.border.subtle.

text.$description: Text light steps (Constitution Article 11 §3). Light follows the claim, not the container. No verdict or brand colour is a text colour.

claim.$description: The verdict word and the decision sentence: the most lit text on a surface.

meta.$description: Windows, bases, clocks and identifiers. Never below 4.5:1 on any surface it can sit on.

border.$description: Rules and boundaries (Constitution Article 18). Structure, never ornament: no border takes a verdict or brand colour.

divider.$description: Separates content. Decorative under WCAG 1.4.11; never the only indicator of a boundary.

subtle.$description: Structural rule or container outline that is not the only indicator of a boundary.

strong.$description: A boundary that is the only indicator of a control (inputs). At least 3:1 on every surface it can sit on.

attention.$description: The single attention signal in a region: the one item that needs a person first. Not a button fill, link, focus ring, selection, success colour, card border, gradient, glow or wash. It does not exist on Off White, where gold measures 2.21:1.

interaction.$description: Interaction roles. These are not verdict roles and not brand roles: every value is a neutral step of light. Brand gold is never an interaction colour (FC-14).

surface.$description: Pointer over an interactive region. Feedback only; carries no meaning.
An item chosen within a set (aria-selected, checked). Never the only indicator: always paired with selected.indicator.

indicator.$description: The non-colour-alone mark of selection. At least 3:1 on every surface.
The current location or open item (aria-current). Not the pressed state, which is interaction.pressed.

ring.$description: The keyboard focus indicator. Neutral, highest contrast, never gold, never a verdict colour. At least 3:1 on every surface.

foreground.$description: The label of a disabled control. WCAG exempts inactive controls; LUMI still holds 3:1. A disabled control always carries its published reason, set in text.meta (STATE_RULES.md §18).

border.$description: The boundary of a disabled control.

verdict.$description: Verdict marks (PR-5, PR-6). A mark sits BESIDE the verdict word; it is never text, never a fill with text inside, never on an action control, never a category palette and never a way to show change between two verdicts (COMPONENT_RULES.md CMP-09). Marks exist only on Charcoal. There are deliberately no verdict text, fill, background or glow tokens.

mark.$description: Resolves through primitive.color.reallocate, never through brand.color.gold.

state.$description: State expression roles (STATE_RULES.md). The backend decides WHICH state is true; these tokens decide only how much light its statement gets. Each state owns its own token even where two share a value, so no state can be restyled by changing another. No state has a tint, wash, fill or icon colour of its own, and no state token is a verdict colour or gold. DISABLED is expressed by color.interaction.disabled.*.

foreground.$description: A value that can be claimed (§2). The reference light for STALE and PARTIAL.
A finding: we looked and there is nothing (§3). An answer, so it is not dimmed like an absence.
We do not know the answer (§4). Lit at claim level, in place, so a failure never reads as calm absence.

border.$description: The in-place boundary of a failed region. At least 3:1.

foreground.$description: The backend reported the claim cannot be provided (§5).
A required connector is not connected (§6). Trigger is PARTIAL (FC-7).
This seat or plan may not ask (§7). Shown locked, never hidden (PR-4).
The question does not apply here (§8).
A measured value past a declared age (§9). Its age sits at the same light as the value; a stale value is never faded.
A published lifecycle stage in flight (§10).
A backend-confirmed terminal success (§11). Neutral: no success colour exists.
Not measured over this window (§12). Structure without light; never a zero.
Data exists and does not meet the bar for the claim (§13).
A sum would be a number in no currency (§15).
A published incompleteness qualifier (§18). The qualifier sits at the same light as the value.

$states.$description: The locked state vocabulary and its expression class. 'value' renders at the light of an available value, 'absence' renders below it (structure without light), 'claim' renders at the highest light, and 'interaction' is expressed by interaction tokens. Checked by tokens.test.js.

$contrast.$description: The contrast-pair manifest (DESIGN_TOKEN_ARCHITECTURE.md §8). Every declared pair is verified per ground at build time. A colour token that is in no pair must be listed in 'exempt' with its reason.

pairs.criterion: LUMI floor for inactive controls (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts them)
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text (focus, selection, current location)
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text (verdict marks and the attention signal)

exempt.color.border.divider: Decorative separator; never the only indicator of a boundary (WCAG 1.4.11 exemption).
exempt.color.border.subtle: Container outline that is never the only indicator of a boundary.
exempt.color.interaction.disabled.border: Boundary of an inactive control (WCAG 1.4.11 exemption).

type.$description: Typography roles (Constitution Article 20). Components consume roles, never sizes. Hierarchy follows DECISION IMPORTANCE > EVIDENCE > CONTEXT, not size alone.

brand.$description: Brand moments on marketing pages. Space Grotesk.

surface.$description: The title of a surface. Space Grotesk, which is rare by rule.

section.$description: A distinct question on a surface. Inter.

claim.$description: The verdict word and the decision sentence. Inter, never smaller than body.default, the most legible words in their region.

default.$description: Windows, bases, clocks and supporting notes. At the legibility floor; never dropped for space.

headline.$description: The headline figure of a claim. JetBrains Mono, tabular. Always rendered with its window.

inline.$description: A figure inside running text or a table row. JetBrains Mono, tabular.

identifier.$description: Identifiers, codes and technical values. JetBrains Mono.

space.$description: Relational spacing tiers (Constitution Article 14). Distance is relationship; each tier doubles the one inside it. A compact object steps down one tier and never below inline (Article 15); compact needs no tokens of its own.

inline.$description: Within one statement: word and mark, value and unit.

meta.$description: A value and its window, basis and clock.

touch.$description: Target for primary actions on touch layouts, which must exceed the minimum (Constitution Article 21).

inline.$description: An icon set within a line of 14px text.

standalone.$description: An icon that is the whole control (close, expand).

offset.$description: Gap between the element and its focus ring.

radius.$description: Radius says what kind of thing an element is (Constitution Article 19). No large radii, no pill token.

round.$description: Only elements round by meaning: an avatar, a radio control.

overlay.$description: The single functional shadow, for surfaces that float over content (menu, popover, dialog). There is no shadow scale and no glow (Constitution Article 18).

motion.$description: Motion foundations only (MOTION_RULES.md). Durations and distances carry a reduced-motion value that replaces them under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. No animation, keyframe or loop tokens exist.

feedback.$description: Acknowledging input. A colour or opacity change, so it survives reduced motion.

reveal.$description: A value becoming known. Instant under reduced motion.

transition.$description: Spatial continuity between views or stages. Instant under reduced motion.

maximum.$description: The ceiling for any UI motion. A limit, not an animation.

settle.$description: The most positional movement a reveal may add. Removed under reduced motion.

layer.$description: The closed stacking order. No numeric z-index outside these tokens.

claim.$description: Maximum width of the primary column that carries the Decision Spine.

evidence.$description: Width of the secondary evidence column.

page.$description: Maximum content width of a surface.

breakpoint.$description: PROVISIONAL. Derived from content widths, not device names (Constitution Article 25). They must be re-measured against the real Decision Spine in Phase 3/4, and laptop must add the persistent navigation width once the app shell fixes it. Not emitted as CSS variables, because a custom property cannot be used in a media query.

tablet.$description: Claim column plus two tablet gutters.

laptop.$description: Claim column plus evidence column plus three desktop gutters.

desktop.$description: Page width plus two desktop gutters.
